notes: The admin app's bundle budget (ADR-0052 §The bundle budget, D10.5).
Bytes are GZIPPED, which is what a browser downloads; `pnpm size` measures dist/ and fails the gate when a number here is exceeded.

js = every JavaScript byte the build emits. css = every CSS byte. entry = the module script dist/index.html loads, the chunk paid before anything renders. chunks = one ceiling per vendor chunk in dist/assets/vendor/ (D14.9).
Raising a budget is a deliberate diff of this file that someone reviews — that is the whole mechanism. Lowering one after a real saving is just as welcome.
The headroom over the baseline is about 8% (11% on css, where a percentage of 14 kB is noise): enough for honest growth, tight enough that a new dependency trips it.

Baseline first measured 2026-08-29 at D10.5, on the tree that already carried D10.3's @dnd-kit and D10.4's stylesheet fix — the first build in which @repo/grid's and @repo/form's utilities actually reach the CSS. Re-measured 2026-08-30 at D11.1; the js and entry numbers moved by 47 and 2 bytes, which is what 'a token re-skin ships no code' looks like from here.

css rose 12598 -> 14042 at D11.1 and its budget with it, deliberately: ADR-0054 §1 self-hosts IBM Plex through @fontsource, and five @fontsource stylesheets (Sans 400/500/600, Mono 400/500, whole faces so unicode-range can do the choosing) carry 28 @font-face rules - ~12.4 kB of very repetitive CSS that gzips to ~1.4 kB. The woff2/woff files themselves are emitted assets and are NOT counted here — a browser downloads only the subsets its text needs, so what this number prices is the declaration, not the faces.

entry is resolved from dist/index.html rather than matched by filename: at D10.5's review an index-*.js pattern was found to match two chunks (the real entry plus an unrelated 0.6 kB one), and it would match zero the day Vite's entryFileNames changes - which would pass green forever.

NOT RAISED at D14.8, which is the outcome ADR-0062 §1 predicted: the composition moved into @repo/app-kit and the same code is still shipped, so `pnpm size` prints js 334.2 / css 14.5 / entry 255.4 kB against 353.5 / 15.2 / 273.4. The one real addition is the top-level error boundary and its crash surface, which is a class component, a paragraph and a button — the ~0.6 kB the entry moved. The next raise this file expects is D14.9's, and it will be a *shape* change rather than a number: per-chunk ceilings beside these totals (ADR-0062 §4).

SHAPE CHANGED at D14.9 (ADR-0062 §4), which is what the D14.8 note said to expect: `chunks` joins `budgets` and `baseline.chunks` joins `baseline`, one ceiling per vendor chunk `vite.config.ts` names, and `scripts/size.mjs` fails on any of them. The mechanism is ADR-0052's and is unchanged — a committed byte count, raised only in a diff someone reviewed.

The entry fell 255.4 -> 159.0 kB on that step, and nothing was removed: `manualChunks` moved React, the router, the query client and the table core out of the entry and into four cacheable chunks. js moved +191 bytes, which is what 'the same bytes in different files' looks like from here.

entry's budget is now 171.9 kB, and it may not be raised past 60% of the js budget — `size.mjs` enforces that arithmetic rather than trusting this note. Before D14.9 the entry was 76% of all JavaScript; the cap is what stops a later step giving that back by editing one number.

The chunk ceilings carry roughly the same headroom the totals do, and `baseline.chunks` records what each one measured on the day it was set — without that, a chunk drifting toward its ceiling is invisible until the day it trips, which is the opposite of what ADR-0052's raise-by-review mechanism is for. react is 59.0 kB and is expected to move only when React does; table is the one to watch, because it is @tanstack/react-table and only the grid uses it.

RE-BASELINED 2026-09-11, after D18 shipped and outside any step, and the first raise of js since D14.9. The reason is that the file had stopped being true: the baseline below still said D14.9's numbers while a cold build measured js 342362 -> 361873 (+19.5 kB), css 14843 -> 14862 (+19 bytes) and entry 162773 -> 166837 (+4.1 kB), the four vendor chunks unmoved to the byte. D18 spent that in this app across D18.6 (the recovery screens), D18.10 (the change-address dialog on both record surfaces) and D18.11 (/onboarding and the passwordless staff create) with no raise and no baseline update, and the ~5% headroom this file is meant to run at had quietly become 0.03% — 353.4 against 353.5 kB as the script prints it. That is not the mechanism failing: nothing went over, so nothing asked anyone to look. It is the baseline going stale, which the D14.9 note above says is exactly what makes drift invisible.

The raise is js 362000 -> 380000 and nothing else: ~5% over the new baseline, the rule the customer file's D15.5 note set and this file has run at since D14.9. css (15600) and entry (176000) are left where they were, both still ~5% over what they measure; the chunk ceilings are untouched because the chunks did not move. The 60%-of-js rule size.mjs enforces is nowhere near binding at 380000.

The lever named at D18.11 is still unpulled: /onboarding and /reset-password are one screen with different copy. This re-baseline buys room; it does not cash that. The +4.1 kB on entry is the eager `en` catalogues ADR-0046 §3 bundles before any lazy import resolves, the same trade the customer file records at D12.8 and D15.5, and entry is the number to watch here too — 5.5% of headroom against 176000.

RAISED at D20.2 — the wave of minor and patch updates ADR-0073 §7 asks for, and the raise is the mechanism working rather than a concession. Nothing about either app changed in this step: what moved is the versions under it, taken to the latest each manifest's range already allowed so `pnpm outdated -r` is left with only D21's four majors.

The one row worth naming is `react`, which is the same chunk in both apps: 60419 -> 69054 (+8.6 kB, +14%). React 19.2.8 -> 19.3.0 is the whole of it, and it is why both budget files are being edited in a step that touched no component. The rest of the growth is spread across zod 4.4.3 -> 4.6.5, lucide-react 1.33 -> 1.47, the three @tanstack packages and react-hook-form 7.85 -> 7.88 — each a few kilobytes, none of them a decision this repository makes.

Every new ceiling is ~5% over the measurement beside it, which is the headroom rule both files have run at since D14.9 and which ADR-0073 §5 is about to make `scripts/size.mjs` enforce at D20.9 (ceiling at most 15% over baseline, re-measured in the diff that raises it). Nothing here is near that cap, and the 60%-of-js rule on the entry is nowhere near binding.

Measured in the bytes this file stores, against the 2026-09-11 re-baseline: js 361873 -> 379434 (+17.6 kB), css 14862 -> 14862 (to the byte), entry 166837 -> 175684 (+8.9 kB), and the chunks query 10598 -> 10386, react 60419 -> 69054, router 28602 -> 28333, table 14039 -> 14041. Two chunks got smaller; react is the whole of the growth.

**Operator-visible**: this app was 566 bytes under its js ceiling and 142 bytes under its entry ceiling before the raise — both would have tripped on the next line of code, which is the drift the 2026-09-11 note says a stale baseline hides. The raise restores ~5% on all three totals. The lever named at D18.11 is still unpulled: /onboarding and /reset-password are one screen with different copy.

RE-BASELINED at D20.9 (ADR-0073 §5), and the first time a ceiling in this file has gone DOWN. Measured in the bytes this file stores, against the D20.2 baseline: js 379434 -> 380323 (+889), css 14862 -> 14911 (+49 bytes, D20.8's reduced-motion rule), entry 175684 -> 160915 (-14.8 kB, -8.4%), the four vendor chunks unmoved to the byte. The entry ceiling is 185000 -> 169000, ~5% over the new measurement; js and css keep their ceilings, both still ~5% over what they measure.

What left the entry, since a lowering has to say as much as a raise: the whole of @dnd-kit (core, sortable, utilities, accessibility — 48 kB of source). Nothing above the routes ever rendered a column menu; the composition root imports `@repo/grid` for its namespace and its lazy catalogue loader, the routes import `list-state` for `validateSearch`, the settings storage imports `preferences` — and every one of those is a barrel import, which until this step dragged every module the barrel re-exports into the entry's graph and kept each one's top-level `createContext`/`forwardRef` calls as side effects. `@repo/grid` and `@repo/form` now declare `sideEffects: false` in their manifests (no module in either runs anything on import — `packages/app-kit`'s composition test asserts the declaration), so Rollup drops the modules nothing reaches. The grid's table itself (`app-grid-<hash>.js`) was already behind the three list routes since D14.9's split and is not what moved.

What did NOT leave, stated so it is not re-litigated: react-hook-form, Radix's select and the floating-ui stack under it (~55 kB of source, ~15 kB gzipped) are still in the entry. The three list route files read their resource config for `editSurfaceOf`, and a typed resource config carries its field adapters (ADR-0063 §1) — the form machinery arrives through the config, not through a barrel, and moving it is a decision about what a route file may read (ADR-0040) rather than a budget setting. It is the next lever on this row and belongs with D22's shared-composition wave. And the `lv` catalogue was never here: ADR-0046 §3 has loaded every non-source locale through `resourcesToBackend` since D7.1, one chunk per `<locale>/<namespace>.json` (`account-<hash>.js`, `common-<hash>.js` and their siblings in dist/assets/), so that half of FE-03's evidence was false when it was written.

The rule this file now runs under (ADR-0073 §5): every ceiling is at most 15% over the baseline beside it, and `scripts/size.mjs` — one script at the repository root since this step, addressed by the directory Turbo runs it in, in place of the copy each app carried — refuses the file otherwise. `scripts/size.test.mjs` reads this file and asserts the rule holds on the committed numbers. A raise past the line is therefore a diff that shows both numbers, which is what the review asked for by name (FE-02).

RE-BASELINED at D21.3 — Vite 8, which bundles with Rolldown in place of Rollup, and nothing about the app changed. Measured in the bytes this file stores, against a cold Vite 7 build of the same tree (not the D20.9 baseline, which D20-D28 had already moved): js 381718 -> 374107, css 14911 -> 14900, entry 159941 -> 167068, and the chunks query 10386 -> 10123, react 69054 -> 67388, router 28333 -> 27102, table 14041 -> 13613. Rolldown's minifier and runtime are what the smaller totals are; every vendor chunk holds the same packages it held under Rollup (`vite.config.ts`'s ranked groups).

THE ENTRY ROW CHANGED ITS FILE SET, not its meaning. Rolldown moves a module the entry shares with a lazy route into a common chunk that dist/index.html preloads, where Rollup kept it in the entry — so the entry *file* fell to about a quarter of what it was while nothing left the first paint. `scripts/size.mjs` now prices the module script plus every non-vendor chunk the page preloads (under Rollup the page preloaded only vendor chunks, so on a Vite 7 build the two definitions give the same number). The Vite 7 figure above is that single file; the rise is the price of the split — per-chunk import and export boilerplate and the runtime chunk, gzipped file by file.

Every ceiling is set again at ~5% over the measurement beside it (4.7% to 5.7%), the rule this file has run at since D14.9 — most of them DOWN, because Rolldown's bundle is smaller and a ceiling left where it was would sit up to 14% over its baseline, one step from ADR-0073 §5's 15% cap and loose enough to hide real growth. Totals: js 399000 -> 393000, and entry 169000 -> 175000 — the one raise, because the new measurement left it 1.2% of headroom. Chunks: query 11500 -> 10700, react 73000 -> 70800, router 31000 -> 28500, table 15200 -> 14300. The 60%-of-js rule on the entry is nowhere near binding.
